strings.d1.s0.name: Acropolis of Athens
strings.d1.s0.tips: The Parthenon. Book a timed online ticket for the 08:00 opening (30 EUR, or 36 EUR for the 7-site combined ticket). In summer it may close from 12:00 to 17:00 because of the heat.
strings.d1.s1.name: Acropolis Museum
strings.d1.s1.tips: A museum with glass floors, the Parthenon frieze and a café with Acropolis views.
strings.d1.s2.name: Plaka
strings.d1.s2.tips: Neoclassical streets at the foot of the Acropolis, plus the white Cycladic-style houses of Anafiotika.
strings.d1.s3.name: Kostas Souvlaki Syntagma
strings.d1.s3.tips: One type of souvlaki since 1950, on Agia Irini square. It closes at 14:00.
strings.d1.s4.name: Anafiotika
strings.d1.s4.tips: An island village tucked against the Acropolis rock, with narrow stairways and cats.
strings.d1.b0.name: O Thanasis Monastiraki
strings.d1.b0.tips: A kebab and pitta classic on Monastiraki square.
strings.d1.b1.name: Areopagus Hill
strings.d1.b1.tips: A rocky hill beside the Acropolis with free views and sunset.
strings.d2.s0.name: Ancient Agora of Athens
strings.d2.s0.tips: Covered by the combined ticket. The Temple of Hephaestus is the best-preserved Greek temple, and the Stoa has a museum.
strings.d2.s1.name: Monastiraki Flea Market
strings.d2.s1.tips: An antiques market on Sundays. On other days the shops are open, around Avissinias square.
strings.d2.s2.name: Roman Agora and Tower of the Winds
strings.d2.s2.tips: Combined ticket. The tower is an octagonal water clock.
strings.d2.s3.name: Varvakios Central Market
strings.d2.s3.tips: The central meat and fish market. The tavernas inside serve patsas (tripe soup) and grilled dishes.
strings.d2.s4.name: Psyrri
strings.d2.s4.tips: A graffiti-covered neighbourhood with cafés and Little Kook, and meyhanes (taverns) in the evening.
strings.d2.b0.name: Diporto Varvakios
strings.d2.b0.tips: A basement taverna with no menu. Chickpeas and fish, cash only.
strings.d2.b1.name: Kerameikos
strings.d2.b1.tips: An ancient cemetery. Combined ticket, and quieter than the Roman Agora.
strings.d3.s0.name: Mount Lycabettus
strings.d3.s0.tips: Take the funicular or climb for 20 minutes. It is the highest point in Athens, with views of the Acropolis and the sea.
strings.d3.s1.name: Kolonaki
strings.d3.s1.tips: A chic neighbourhood with cafés along Skoufa street.
strings.d3.s2.name: Benaki Museum
strings.d3.s2.tips: Greek history and crafts in a mansion, with a terrace café.
strings.d3.s3.name: National Archaeological Museum
strings.d3.s3.tips: The Mycenaean gold mask and the Antikythera mechanism. Air-conditioned, so good for the midday heat.
strings.d3.s4.name: Exarcheia
strings.d3.s4.tips: An anarchist and student neighbourhood with record shops and rebetiko bars.
strings.d3.b0.name: Philos Athens Kolonaki
strings.d3.b0.tips: Brunch in Kolonaki, as a lunch alternative to the museum.
strings.d3.b1.name: Museum of Cycladic Art
strings.d3.b1.tips: Cycladic idols, as an alternative to the Benaki.
strings.d4.s0.name: Lake Vouliagmeni
strings.d4.s0.tips: One hour by tram and bus. A thermal lake with fish pedicures, and 22°C even in winter.
strings.d4.s1.name: Kavouri Coastal Walk
strings.d4.s1.tips: A pine-lined coastal path in Kavouri, with winter sun.
strings.d4.s2.name: Ithaki Restaurant Vouliagmeni
strings.d4.s3.name: Glyfada Centre
strings.d4.s3.tips: The Riviera's shopping district. Return by tram.
strings.d4.s4.name: Flisvos Marina
strings.d4.s4.tips: A marina promenade and sunset spot, with the Averof battleship.
strings.d4.b0.name: Akrogiali Vouliagmeni
strings.d4.b1.name: Stavros Niarchos Foundation Park
strings.d4.b1.tips: A Renzo Piano park and opera house, as an alternative to Flisvos.
strings.d5.s0.name: Lavrio Archaeological Museum
strings.d5.s0.tips: In an ancient silver-mining town on the way, 1.5 hours from Athens by KTEL bus.
strings.d5.s1.name: Akrogiali Sounion Taverna
strings.d5.s1.tips: A fish taverna in the bay with views of the temple.
strings.d5.s2.name: Sounion Beach
strings.d5.s3.name: Temple of Poseidon Sounion
strings.d5.s3.tips: A temple on the cape. Arrive at 17:30 for sunset (16:30 in winter). Byron's signature is carved on a column.
strings.d5.b0.name: Cape Sounion Sunset Café
strings.d5.b0.tips: A café next to the temple.
strings.d5.b1.name: Lavrio Port
strings.d5.b1.tips: A fishing harbour, as an alternative to the museum.
strings.d6.s0.name: Aegina Port
strings.d6.s0.tips: A 40-minute ferry from Piraeus (about 10 EUR). The pistachio island, with horse-drawn carriages.
strings.d6.s1.name: Temple of Aphaia
strings.d6.s1.tips: A Doric temple on a hilltop in Aegina, older than the Parthenon.
strings.d6.s2.name: Agia Marina Aegina
strings.d6.s2.tips: A sandy beach and village, good for a winter walk.
strings.d6.s3.name: Skotadis Aegina
strings.d6.s3.tips: A fish taverna on the harbour, with pistachio desserts.
strings.d6.s4.name: Aegina Pistachio Market
strings.d6.s4.tips: Buy Aegina pistachios as souvenirs. The ferry leaves at 17:00.
strings.d6.b0.name: Aegina Miltos Balık
strings.d6.b1.name: Paleochora Aegina
strings.d7.theme: Panathenaic and National Garden: a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Panathenaic Stadium
strings.d7.s0.tips: A marble Olympic stadium. Run on the track.
strings.d7.s1.name: National Garden Athens
strings.d7.s1.tips: A royal garden with palms and turtles, next to the Zappeion.
strings.d7.s2.name: Syntagma Changing of the Guard
strings.d7.s2.tips: The Evzones guards change every hour. On Sundays at 11:00 there is a large ceremony.
strings.d7.s3.name: Ta Karamanlidika tou Fani
strings.d7.s3.tips: A deli and meyhane (tavern). Pastirma (cured beef) and cheese platter for a farewell.
strings.d7.s4.name: Syntagma Metro Airport
strings.d7.s4.tips: The airport metro takes 40 minutes. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Feyrouz Athens
strings.d7.b0.tips: Lahmacun (thin Turkish flatbread with minced meat) and cheese pides. A quick farewell meal.
strings.d7.b1.name: Temple of Olympian Zeus
strings.d7.b1.tips: Combined ticket. Giant columns, as an alternative to the stadium.
strings.note0: The metro has 3 lines; the airport metro takes 40 minutes and costs 10 EUR. Take the tram to the Riviera, a KTEL bus to Sounion (Pedion Areos), and a Piraeus ferry to the islands.
strings.note1: The Acropolis costs 30 EUR with a timed online ticket. The 7-site combined ticket costs 36 EUR (valid for 5 days). Entry is free on the first Sunday (November to March).
strings.note2: Winter is sunny at 10-15°C, with no crowds. Lake Vouliagmeni stays warm in winter, and sunset at Sounion is at 17:00.
strings.note3: Souvlaki costs 4-5 EUR and a taverna meal 15-25 EUR. Drink freddo espresso as your coffee, and round up the bill as a tip; there is no coperto (cover charge).
strings.note4: Watch for pickpockets on the metro and in Monastiraki. Omonia is quiet at night.
strings.note5: On Sundays there is the Monastiraki flea market and the Syntagma ceremony. Museums may be closed on Tuesdays.
